name: Metformin Contraindication in Severe Renal Impairment
description: Metformin is strictly contraindicated in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m² due to high risk of fatal lactic acidosis.
guideline_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

conclusions.name: Metformin Severe Renal Contraindication
conclusions.explanation: Patient has eGFR < 30 mL/min and is taking Metformin. High risk of fatal lactic acidosis. Immediately discontinue Metformin and evaluate alternative antidiabetic agents (e.g., SGLT2i or Insulin).

provenance.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

name: Metformin Dose Capping in Moderate Renal Impairment
description: Patients with eGFR between 30 and 45 mL/min/1.73m² must not exceed 1000 mg/day of Metformin with eGFR monitored every 3-6 months.
guideline_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

conclusions.name: Metformin Dose Capping Required
conclusions.explanation: Patient eGFR is between 30 and 45 mL/min. Cap Metformin dose at 1000 mg/day maximum and schedule renal function tests every 3-6 months.

provenance.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

name: ACEi and Spironolactone Dual Hyperkalemia Risk
description: Concurrent ACE-inhibitor (Lisinopril) or ARB with Spironolactone substantially increases the risk of severe hyperkalemia.
section: Critical Drug Interactions and Hyperkalemia Risk

conclusions.name: Severe Hyperkalemia Interaction Risk
conclusions.explanation: Concurrent administration of Lisinopril (ACEi) and Spironolactone (potassium-sparing diuretic) elevates hyperkalemia risk. Frequent serum potassium and creatinine monitoring is mandatory.

provenance.guideline: AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guidelines (2023)
provenance.section: Critical Drug Interactions and Hyperkalemia Risk

name: Critical Serum Potassium Elevation Alert
description: Serum potassium >= 5.5 mEq/L represents dangerous hyperkalemia requiring urgent clinical intervention.

conclusions.name: Critical Hyperkalemia Alert
conclusions.explanation: Serum potassium is >= 5.5 mEq/L. Immediately withhold potassium-sparing diuretics, ACEi/ARBs, evaluate 12-lead ECG, and institute potassium-lowering therapy.

provenance.guideline: AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guidelines (2023)

name: Stage 2 Essential Hypertension Diagnostic Assessment
description: Systolic BP >= 140 mmHg or Diastolic BP >= 90 mmHg meets criteria for Stage 2 Hypertension.
section: Diagnostic Criteria and Blood Pressure Thresholds

conclusions.name: Stage 2 Hypertension Confirmed
conclusions.explanation: Blood pressure measurements meet criteria for Stage 2 Hypertension (SBP >= 140 or DBP >= 90 mmHg). Dual first-line antihypertensive therapy (ACEi/ARB + CCB or Diuretic) indicated.

provenance.guideline: AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guidelines (2023)
provenance.section: Diagnostic Criteria and Blood Pressure Thresholds

name: ACEi/ARB Renal Protection Indication in Diabetic Nephropathy
description: Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and CKD (eGFR < 60) should receive ACEi or ARB therapy for renoprotection unless contraindicated.
guideline_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

conclusions.name: Renoprotective ACEi/ARB Indicated
conclusions.explanation: Patient has Type 2 Diabetes with renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min) but is not currently prescribed an ACEi or ARB. Initiate Lisinopril or Losartan to reduce proteinuria and delay CKD progression.

provenance.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

name: SGLT2 Inhibitor Cardiorenal Benefit Indication
description: SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin) are strongly recommended in patients with Type 2 Diabetes and established Heart Failure or CKD.
guideline_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

conclusions.name: SGLT2 Inhibitor Indication for Heart Failure
conclusions.explanation: Patient has comorbid Type 2 Diabetes and Heart Failure with adequate renal reserve (eGFR >= 20). Add Empagliflozin for documented reduction in heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality.

provenance.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

name: Uncontrolled Glycemia (HbA1c >= 8.0%)
description: HbA1c >= 8.0% indicates sub-optimal glycemic control and increased microvascular complication risks.
guideline_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

conclusions.name: Suboptimal Glycemic Control
conclusions.explanation: Patient's HbA1c is >= 8.0% (target < 7.0%). Review medication adherence, dietary habits, and consider antidiabetic therapy intensification.

provenance.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024)

name: Serum Potassium Monitoring Requirement for ACEi Therapy
